MRS . JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard the arguments of both the sides.
2. These appeals are filed against the judgment and award passed in M.V.C.No.3064/2022 dated 12.07.2024 by the Court of Small Causes, Member Prl. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Bengaluru.

sentences.text: 3. The deceased E-Chaithanya, aged 15 years has met with an accident on 15.05.2022 and subsequently, his parents filed a claim petition claiming compensation of 25,00,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the facts and circumstance and evidence on record, has awarded the compensation of Rs.17,95,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the petition till realization.
4. Aggrieved by the said order, the Insurance company preferred appeal in MFA.No.6078/2024 and NC: 2026:KHC:13380 HC-KAR mainly contented that the deceased was studying in 9th Standards.
The Tribunal considered his notional income as Rs.15,500/- as he was a minor and non-earning member.

The Tribunal ought to have granted Rs.5,00,000/- towards loss of dependency relying on Sri E Ashok vs Smt Bhaskar Banu Ramani on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103798938/
4

sentences.text: The compensation granted is on higher side and thus, the Insurance Company requested for reduction of the same.

5. Against the same judgment and award, the claimants also filed MFA.No.8440/2024 and they contended that future prospects of 40% is not considered by the Tribunal while calculating the loss of dependency and interest granted at the rate of 6% is on lesser side.
Thus, they requested for enhancement of the compensation.
NC: 2026:KHC:13380 HC-KAR 6.
The deceased E. Chaithanya was aged 15 years.
He met with an accident on 15.05.2022.
As there is no income proof, his notional income was rightly considered by the Tribunal as Rs.15,500/- as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
As he was aged 15 years, the multiplier is to be taken as '18'.

He is entitled for the future prospects at 40%, as he was a bachelor,
50% is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then towards 'loss of dependency' it would come to an amount of Rs.23,43,600/- (15,500 + 40% X 12 X 18-50%).
7.

Parents are entitled for 'consortium' of Rs.44,000/- by each of them i.e., Rs.88,000/-
(Rs.44,000/- X 2) and Rs.33,000/- under 'the conventional heads'.

8. Thus, in all, compensation awarded by this Court is as below:
NC: 2026:KHC:13380 HC-KAR Sl.Nos.
Particulars Amount in Rs. 1 Towards loss of dependency 23,43,600/- 2
Towards loss of consortium 88,000/- 3
Towards conventional heads 33,000/-
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.17,95,000/-.

Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.6,69,600/-
(Rs.24,64,600/- - Rs.17,95,000/-).
10.

In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER i.
The appeal in MFA.No.6078/2024 is dismissed.
ii. The appeal in MFA.No.8440/2024 is allowed in part.

iii. The judgment and award dated 29.09.2023 passed in M.V.C.No.3064/2022 dated 12.07.2024 by the Court of Small Causes, NC: 2026:KHC:13380 HC-KAR Member Prl. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Bengaluru, is modified.
